captions: Part five. Trust, and memory.
How the harness checks every number, and learns
from every correction.
Now the gate that makes this trustworthy.
The verifier pulls every number out of the
draft and looks for it in the evidence
log.
Net margin rose from 7.32 percent. Found.
To 8.50 now. Found.
Revenue grew 10.4 percent. Not found. The model
estimated that in its head.
The verifier sends it back, the model calls
the tool, and the real figure is 14.07
percent.
Debt to equity fell to 0.25. Found.
Zero uncited numbers. Only now does the answer
go out.
Matching numbers catches most errors. A few simple
rules catch the rest.
Units: a hundred times jump is almost always
a unit slip.
Ranges: margins stay within plus or minus a
hundred percent.
Periods must be contiguous.
Conflicts are shown, not hidden.
Every answer states its as-of date.
And refusal is a feature. Not in the
loaded documents is a far better answer than
a guess.
How do you know it works? Build a
golden set before adding clever features.
About fifty questions across a few companies, mixing
lookups, trends, ratios, cross-source checks, narrative whys, and
questions it should refuse.
Numbers are graded exactly, within a small tolerance.
For narrative answers you'll use an LLM judge.
But validate that judge against human labels first.
In one public FinanceBench write-up, an unchecked judge
inflated scores by thirty four percent.
Now memory, just like the Mem0 system from
our last video.
Working memory is this session's evidence. Short-term memory
is the conversation. Preferences are durable facts about
the user.
The most valuable layer is tribal knowledge: corrections
the agent learned the hard way, each stored
with a condition for when it applies.
A 2026 paper called Tk-Boost did exactly this
for SQL agents, and improved accuracy by up
to sixteen point nine percent on Spider two.
One rule. Never keep financial numbers in memory.
They live in the facts table, with provenance.
Here's how a correction becomes a skill.
The user corrects the agent: those borrowings are
in lakh.
After the session, the harness extracts a learning,
with a condition: when the source is this
broker's file.
It's stored, and like Mem0, it's compared with
existing memories first, to add, update, or skip.
Next session, any question touching that file will
recall it in the context builder.
The same mistake never happens twice.
